P1_pole_eigenstructure.note: C high => poles share one direction (common tilted plane / shepherd or fixed frame); G high => poles on a great circle (warped disk / inclination instability). Null holds i fixed, om uniform -- the ecliptic ring it produces is itself girdle-like.

P2_common_plane.note: pole azimuth = mean(Omega) - 90 deg, so this largely restates the node clustering; the new information is the eigenstructure (P1): a point excess, no girdle -- a common tilted plane, not a warped disk

P3_perihelion_eigenstructure.note: perihelion vectors are point-like not axial; C tests extra point-concentration beyond the conditioned null
